verses.text: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and very upset. He made fun of the Jews.

In front of his friends and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these weak Jews doing? Do they think they can rebuild the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish it in one day? Can they bring these burned stones back to life from the piles of rubble?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was standing beside him. He said, "Even if a fox climbed up on what they are building, it would knock their stone wall down!"
I prayed, "Listen, our God, because we are being looked down on. Turn their insults back on their own heads. Let them be carried off as prisoners to a foreign land.
Do not cover up their guilt or wipe out their sins from your sight, because they have insulted the builders."
So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, because the people worked with all their hearts.
But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls were going ahead and that the gaps were being closed. They were very angry.
They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause trouble.
But we prayed to our God and posted guards day and night to protect ourselves from them.
Meanwhile the people of Judah said, "The workers are getting tired, and there is too much rubble. We cannot rebuild the wall."
Our enemies said, "Before they know it or see us, we will be right among them. We will kill them and stop the work."
The Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times over, "They will attack us from every direction."
So I placed people behind the lowest parts of the wall, in the open places. I placed them by families, with their swords, spears, and bows.

After I looked things over, I stood up and said to the important men, the officials, and the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, who is great and amazing. Fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes."
Our enemies heard that we knew about their plot and that God had ruined their plans. So we all went back to the wall, each to our own work.
From that day on, half of my men did the work, while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stood behind all the people of Judah
who were building the wall. Those who carried loads did their work with one hand and held a weapon in the other.
Each of the builders wore his sword at his side while he worked. The man who blew the trumpet stayed with me.
I said to the important men, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is big and spread out, and we are far apart from each other along the wall.
Wherever you hear the trumpet, come and join us there. Our God will fight for us!"
So we kept working, with half the men holding spears, from the first light of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also told the people, "Every man and his helper should stay inside Jerusalem at night. Then they can guard us at night and work during the day."
So none of us took off our clothes, not I, my brothers, my servants, or the guards with me. Each of us kept our weapon with us, even when we went for water.
